[PERSISTENT EXPERIENCE GUIDANCE]
## Consolidated Experience from Similar Tasks
Across all cases, failures arose from assuming that a subsequent action would succeed without verifying its preconditions. The generalizable lessons are: (1) Movement preconditions - before issuing a move command, verify the intended path is clear of obstacles; if blocked (e.g., a stool), do not assume forward motion will succeed, but instead navigate around, remove, or replan the route. (2) Pickup preconditions - before attempting a pick, confirm the target object actually exists, is visible, and is within reach; if it is not nearby, navigate to its location first. (3) Place preconditions - before attempting a place, confirm the robot is actually holding the target object (i.e., a successful pick has occurred); never place an object that is not in the gripper. In short: model the preconditions of every action and satisfy them before execution, rather than chaining actions on optimistic assumptions.

## Preliminary Thinking
Break the request into ordered sub-tasks and verify preconditions at each step: (1) Navigate to the bed for tidying, first checking the path for obstacles and replanning around any blockage (as with the stool case). (2) Tidy the bed (e.g., clear/straighten items) to prepare a surface. (3) Locate the book and navigate to its position, confirming it exists, is visible, and is reachable before acting. (4) Perform the pick-up action, ensuring the robot is close enough to succeed. (5) Confirm the robot is actually holding the book before proceeding. (6) Navigate back to the bed and place the book on it, only after verifying the hold. If any precondition fails (blocked path, object not reachable, empty gripper), diagnose and correct it (replan, navigate, or re-pick) instead of executing the next action blindly.
[/PERSISTENT EXPERIENCE GUIDANCE]
